name: Lafcadio Hearn
nationality: Greek and Irish by birth; a Japanese citizen from 1896 as Koizumi Yakumo
knownFor: The writer who carried Japanese ghost stories into English.

works.title: Chita: A Memory of Last Island
works.note: a novella after the hurricane of 1856

works.title: Two Years in the French West Indies
works.note: from his two years in Martinique

works.title: Kokoro: Hints and Echoes of Japanese Inner Life
Kwaidan: Stories and Studies of Strange Things
works.note: his best-known book of ghost stories

events.text: Born on Lefkada to a Greek mother and an Anglo-Irish army-surgeon father; raised in Dublin by a great-aunt.
Sent to the United States at nineteen, and for a time lived by odd jobs in Cincinnati.
Began as a reporter on the Cincinnati Daily Enquirer, where he stayed until 1875.
Moved to New Orleans, where he wrote for the Daily City Item and then the Times Democrat for nearly a decade.
Harper's sent him to Martinique as a correspondent; he stayed two years.
Went to Japan on a newspaper commission that ended almost at once, and found a teaching post instead; he never left.
Became a Japanese citizen under the name Koizumi Yakumo, and took up lecturing at the Imperial University in Tokyo.
Kwaidan appeared in the year he died of heart failure in Tokyo, aged 54.

relevance: Kwaidan retells ghost stories and legends drawn from Japanese books and from what Hearn heard in Japan, in an English plain enough to be read aloud. It is the most direct route in English into that strand of Japanese folk tradition.
influence: His books were translated into Japanese and remain popular there. Matsue, Yaizu and Hearn's birthplace of Lefkada each keep a museum or memorial centre for him.
